newsitem.title: USA: Apache Egyptian well tests 104 mmcf/g a day.
newsitem.headline: Apache Egyptian well tests 104 mmcf/g a day.

text.p: Apache Corp on Wednesday said its Shams-2x Khalda gas well in Egypt's Western Desert tested at an aggregate daily rate of about 104 million cubic feet of gas and 1,606 barrels of condensate on a 3/4-inch choke.
Apache has a 40-percent contractor interest in the Khalda Concession. Repsol SA owns 50 percent and Samsung Co holds the remaining 10 percent.
The producer will add to reserves dedicated to a 200 MMcf per day contract to supply gas to Egypt's energy grid.
Apache said that engineering studies are under way for a potential second gas pipeline connecting the concession with existing facilities to the south and east.
The Khalda gas contract is for a term of 25 years, commencing May 1, 1999. Apache's share of the production is 80 MMcf per day, the company said.
